title.en: Explain objectives, strategy, policy, procedure, method, rule, programme and budget

say.en: "No mobile phones in the lab" and "Raise sales by 20 percent" are both plans, but of very different kinds. Let us sort the plans a manager uses. In this lesson: Distinguish single-use and standing plans.
Explain objectives, strategy, policy, procedure, method, rule, programme and budget.

body.en: Single-use plans are made for a one-time event or project, such as a programme or a budget for an exhibition. *Standing plans* are used again and again for repeated situations, such as policies, procedures, methods and rules.

narration.en: Single-use plans are made for a one-time event or project, such as a programme or a budget for an exhibition. Standing plans are used again and again for repeated situations, such as policies, procedures, methods and rules.

body.en: Objectives are the end results. Strategy is a comprehensive plan to achieve objectives, considering the environment. A policy is a general guide to thinking. A procedure is a sequence of routine steps. A method is the prescribed way of doing a task. A rule says what must or must not be done. A programme is a detailed plan for a project. A budget is a plan in numbers.

problem.en: Classify: (a) "We will recruit only through campus placements." (b) "Wear safety shoes in the plant." (c) Steps to process a leave application. (d) Sales of ₹50 lakh expected next quarter.

steps.en: (a) A general guide for recruitment decisions: policy.
(b) Must be followed with no discretion: rule.
(c) A sequence of routine steps: procedure.
(d) An expected result in numbers: budget.

answer.en: Policy, rule, procedure and budget respectively.
